candidate.title: Hosting a quirky book swap party
candidate.scenario: You’re organizing a small, casual book swap for six friends over pizza at your apartment on Saturday evening. Your apartment has a small dining table, a cozy couch, and a bookshelf cluttered with 15 personal books you’d miss if sold. Everyone loves rare editions and genre-specific reads, but budget is tight—you’ve set aside $30 for supplies. One friend, Priya, has a mild sensitivity to strong smells, and another, Leo, prefers discussions over games. Your goal is to ensure everyone leaves with at least two books while keeping costs low and avoiding sensory triggers.
candidate.user_persona: You’re a 28-year-old avid reader who loves hosting but struggles with logistics. You’re detail-oriented, a little competitive about finding unique books, and enjoy testing group dynamics with unconventional ideas. You’re also thrifty, but won’t skimp on comfort for your guests.
candidate.assistant_mode: Remote text helper. I’ll help you brainstorm how to curate the book swap, prioritizing your constraints and guest preferences without exceeding $30 on supplies. We’ll focus on maximizing the experience for everyone while keeping your apartment functional and Priya/Leo’s comfort in mind.
candidate.goal: Select 12 books from your collection to swap (6 for guests, 6 to keep), identify 3 alternative books to offer for guests who don’t find a fit, and plan one activity to engage Leo and Priya without games or strong scents. Use only your existing $30 budget, the apartment’s furniture, and the books you’ve listed as personal favorites.
candidate.resolution: You’ll swap the 6 books you least cherish (*‘The Stranger’* by Camus, *‘Dune’* by Herbert, *‘Beloved’* by Morrison, *‘One Hundred Years of Solitude’* by García Márquez, *‘The Bell Jar’* by Plath, and *‘Pale Fire’* by Nabokov). You’ll offer 3 additional books (your well-read *‘Slaughterhouse-Five’* for humor, *‘The Poisonwood Bible’* for debate, and *‘Mexican Gothic’* for eerie appeal) alongside your 6 favorites for Leo to browse. To engage Priya and Leo, you’ll host a ‘blind book description’ game where guests guess titles based on your 1-minute summaries—no gamesheets or strong smells involved. Your $30 covers a lavender-scented candle (for you) and a $20 pizza order from *Chez Pierre*, a local spot with mild cheese aromas. The small dining table hosts the books; the couch and bookshelf remain free for guests to relax.
facts: Your apartment’s dining table seats six comfortably but won’t hold more than 12 books without clutter.
Priya avoids strong smells but enjoys light perfumes or candles (you’ll use a lavender candle, priced at $8).
Leo prefers discussion-based activities and won’t engage in competitive games.
You’ve budgeted $30 total for supplies, including food and decorations.
Chez Pierre serves $12 personal pizzas with mild cheese aromas and is walkable from your apartment.

You own 15 personal books but can part with the least cherished 6 (*‘The Stranger’*–Camus, *‘Dune’*–Herbert, *‘Beloved’*–Morrison, *‘One Hundred Years of Solitude’*–García Márquez, *‘The Bell Jar’*–Plath, *‘Pale Fire’*–Nabokov). You also have *‘Slaughterhouse-Five’*, *‘The Poisonwood Bible’*, and *‘Mexican Gothic’* that guests might enjoy but aren’t your top 6 to keep.
